notes: Major disagreement on protein microarray screen validity. LLM finds the systematic screen (1321 TFs, 154 motifs) with acknowledged ~27% false positive rate sufficient. Peer reviewers express concern about screening method reliability and request more detailed discussion of false positive/negative rates, indicating uncertainty about the breadth and accuracy of TF identification.

Both agree on dual-specificity TF findings. The identification of 17 TFs binding both methylated and unmethylated DNA with distinct sequence preferences, validated by EMSA for KLF4, TFAP2A, ARID3B, and ZMYM3, is accepted by both evaluators without challenge.

Disagreement on competition EMSA evidence for KLF4's separate binding domains. LLM finds the competitive vs. non-competitive binding patterns convincing. Peer reviewers note Figure 2F lacks negative controls and request experiments with both methylated and unmethylated competitor DNA added simultaneously, indicating incomplete evidence.

Disagreement on OIRD binding affinity data. LLM finds KD values (460, 399, 479 nM) comparable to MBD2b sufficient validation. Peer reviewers request more comprehensive biochemical characterization and comparison to published affinities for multiple TF-meCpG interactions, indicating current data insufficient.

Disagreement on molecular dissection of KLF4 dual-specificity. LLM finds MD simulation predictions and mutagenesis validation (R458A, D460A abolishing mCpG binding while preserving CpG binding) rigorous. Peer reviewers want further dissection to identify which specific domain/zinc finger mediates unmethylated DNA binding, indicating mechanistic understanding is incomplete.

Both agree on luciferase assay functional validation. The demonstration that KLF4 mutations (R458A, D460A) abolish methylated DNA-dependent transcriptional activation while preserving unmethylated DNA activity is accepted by both evaluators without critique.

Major disagreement on in vivo ChIP validation. LLM finds ChIP-bisulfite sequencing showing KLF4 binding to methylated CCCpGCC sites (methylation enrichment p=0.001, p=0.04) comprehensive and rigorous. Peer reviewers express major concern about physiological relevance, cite poor quality/presentation of ChIP-seq data in Figure 4A, and request ChIP-qPCR to convince readers KLF4 is actually bound in vivo. Reviewers state authors must better demonstrate dual preference in vivo before publication.

Disagreement on ZNF114/ZNF416 as novel generic methylated DNA-binding proteins. LLM finds identification well-supported by microarray data showing binding to nearly all motifs. Peer reviewers question why these proteins weren't identified in previous screenings, requesting better contextualization and validation, expressing uncertainty about the novelty claim.

Disagreement on comparison to prior literature. LLM finds the transparent assessment of limitations and comparison with Spruijt et al. (5/11 overlap) appropriately critical. Peer reviewers find comparison incomplete, requesting discussion of overlap/discrepancies/novelties and specifically asking why Rfx proteins weren't identified, indicating uncertainty about how findings relate to existing literature.

Partial overlap on EMSA validation. LLM R2 focuses on validation of 8/11 TFs (73% rate) and competition experiments. Peer R1 includes C32 (competition EMSA) but groups it with broader screening concerns about false positive/negative rates, leading to UNCERTAIN status for the overall screening approach.

Minimal overlap (C24 only). LLM R10 addresses binding specificity patterns showing 15% broad binders vs. sequence-dependent binders. Peer R8 includes C24 in context of questioning why ZNF114/ZNF416 weren't previously identified. Different focus areas with limited claim overlap.

LLM finds HOXA5/DIDO1 luciferase validation UNCERTAIN due to heterologous cell system (GT1-7 cells) and artificial reporter construct. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims (C15, C35, C36).

LLM finds statistical enrichment of mCpG-binding TFs for oncogenes/tumor suppressors (p<0.01) and developmental factors (p<0.015) well-supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for claims C28, C29.

LLM finds discussion of study limitations (limited motif coverage, exclusion of CHG/CHH methylation, hemimethylated DNA, unconventional DNA-binding proteins) appropriately scoped. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for claims C79-C83.

LLM finds broader implications about methylated cytosines as 'fifth alphabet' (C96, C99, C100) intellectually compelling but somewhat speculative, requiring additional genome-wide studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these conceptual claims.
